review_notes: I read all of Inertia.lean. It has one theorem, with no simp attributes, no new definitions and no rewrite rules. I checked the simp lemma it uses. `doubleCosetQuotientEquivPrimesOverOfIsInvariant_mk` in Invariant/Basic.lean is already `@[simp]` and oriented sensibly, from the class of σ to `(σ • Q).under C`. I also checked `ramificationIdx_under_smul_eq_relIndex_inertia` in HilbertTheory/IntermediateRing.lean and the downstream uses in SpecialCases.lean. Those uses rewrite with `_mk_one` and then apply lemmas directly, so none of them needs a simp-normal form of the target's formula. The target's statement uses `q.out`. That choice is deliberate and explained in the docstring. A `DoubleCoset.mk`-form variant could be added, but nothing in the sources shows a use that needs it, so I did not report it. I found no competing rules, no cycles and no unwanted expansion. I did not run Lean, so I can't rule out simp issues that only appear at elaboration time.
